purpose: Metolazone helps your body get rid of extra fluid and salt by making you urinate more. It is used to treat high blood pressure and swelling (edema) caused by heart failure, kidney disease, or liver problems. Reducing extra fluid helps lower your blood pressure and makes it easier for your heart to work.
how_it_works: Your kidneys filter your blood and control how much salt and water stay in your body. Metolazone works by telling your kidneys to release more salt and water into your urine instead of keeping it in your body. As your body loses this extra fluid, your blood pressure goes down and swelling is reduced.
common_side_effects: You may notice you need to urinate more often, especially after taking your dose. Other common side effects include dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly), muscle cramps or weakness, feeling tired, dry mouth, and low potassium levels which can cause weakness or irregular heartbeat.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you feel very dizzy, faint, have a rapid or irregular heartbeat, severe muscle weakness, or urinate much less than usual. This medicine can lower potassium and sodium levels in your blood, so your doctor may check blood tests regularly. Avoid getting up too fast to prevent falls from dizziness. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially other blood pressure drugs, digoxin, or lithium. Do not use if you are allergic to sulfa drugs without checking with your doctor first.
typical_dosing: For high blood pressure, the usual dose is 2.5 to 5 mg taken by mouth once a day in the morning. For swelling (edema), doses can range from 5 to 20 mg once daily. Always take it in the morning to avoid waking up at night to urinate. Your doctor will find the right dose for you based on your condition.
